QuestionStmt.S: Assume the cell reaction, $$A_{(s)} + B_{(aq)}^{2+} \rightarrow A_{(aq)}^{2+} + B_{(s)}$$ if $\Delta G^\circ = -386$ kJ at 298 K. What is $E_{\text{Cell}}^\circ$?

Solution.S:
Cell reaction: $A_{(s)} + B_{(aq)}^{2+} \rightarrow A_{(aq)}^{2+} + B_{(s)}$.

$\Delta G^\circ = -386 \times 10^3$ J at 298 K.

Number of electrons transferred: $n = 2$.

Using $\Delta G^\circ = -nF E_{\text{cell}}^\circ$:

$$-386 \times 10^3 = -2 \times 96500 \times E_{\text{cell}}^\circ$$

$$E_{\text{cell}}^\circ = \frac{386 \times 10^3}{2 \times 96500} = \frac{386000}{193000} = 2 \text{ V}$$

Thus the correct option is C: 2 V.
